entities.summary:
The Third Punic War was a pivotal conflict between Rome and Carthage from 149 to 146 BCE, taking place in Tunisia. This war was significant because it marked the end of the Punic Wars and the destruction of Carthage, a major power in the Mediterranean. The war was sparked by Rome's desire to assert its dominance over the region and eliminate the Carthaginian threat. The war saw the Roman general Scipio Aemilianus crush the Carthaginian forces at the Battle of Carthage, leading to the sacking and destruction of the city. The war had far-reaching consequences, including the eventual Roman conquest of the Mediterranean and the establishment of Rome as the dominant power in the region. The legacy of the Third Punic War can be seen in the rise of Rome as a world power and the decline of Carthage as a major force in the Mediterranean.

The war also had significant cultural and economic consequences, including the spread of Roman culture and the decline of Carthaginian trade and commerce.
